hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a small deterministic alias map for technical synonyms in `solution.py` and normalize mapped terms before matching; this will improve exact-match quality on DEV if synonymous wording is the main remaining source of mismatch.
hypothesis.rationale: The authoritative TASK.md describes matching short technical position statements to canonical engineering concepts and names synonyms as a potential error class. Prior token normalization, stopword filtering, and overlap tie-break experiments each showed only small partial gains, so alias equivalence tests a distinct lexical mechanism.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Quality increases by at least 0.001 versus the current champion on the fixed DEV set.
hypothesis.falsification_condition: Reject the mechanism if the DEV quality delta is below 0.001 or alias normalization causes no measurable increase in correct exact matches.
hypothesis.novelty_rationale: This tests explicit synonym equivalence, a new mechanism family relative to experiments 1–3. Those experiments recorded partial DEV gains of 0.0002, 0.0003, and 0.0004 respectively; each was rejected for not meeting the minimum promotion threshold, so their results support continued changes to lexical matching but do not establish alias mapping as effective.

candidates.suspected_failure_mode: Semantically equivalent technical terms may have little or no token overlap with the canonical concept.
candidates.predicted_observable: Ablation and DEV comparison show that examples differing primarily by a known synonym are newly matched correctly, with total quality improving by at least 0.001.
candidates.discriminating_test: Compare the alias map enabled versus disabled on the same fixed DEV set; inspect whether corrected examples contain mapped synonymous terms and whether quality delta meets the threshold.
candidates.rationale: Within the allowed file and task scope, this directly tests the named synonym error class. Implementation effort can be bounded to a small explicit map.
candidates.uncertainty: No supplied evidence identifies which DEV errors are synonym mismatches, so the expected benefit is plausible but unverified.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Make matching sensitive to negation cues and their nearby technical terms in `solution.py`; this will improve exact-match quality if the current overlap score treats opposite-polarity statements as equivalent.
hypothesis.rationale: The authoritative TASK.md and project context identify negation as a potential error class. A polarity feature changes how token overlap is interpreted and is materially distinct from token normalization, stopword filtering, and tie-breaking.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Quality increases by at least 0.001 versus the current champion on the fixed DEV set, particularly on statements whose meaning reverses under negation.
hypothesis.falsification_condition: Reject if the fixed DEV quality delta is below 0.001 or negation-bearing examples do not show fewer polarity-confusion errors.
hypothesis.novelty_rationale: This is a new semantic-polarity mechanism family. Experiments 1–3 had partial quality gains of 0.0002–0.0004 but all missed promotion; those measured results indicate existing overlap refinements have not yet crossed the threshold, without showing that negation is responsible for the residual errors.

candidates.suspected_failure_mode: Statements with opposing polarity may score similarly because negation words have low weight or are omitted from overlap decisions.
candidates.predicted_observable: Negation-bearing DEV examples with opposing meanings are less often matched to the same canonical concept, and aggregate quality rises by at least 0.001.
candidates.discriminating_test: On the fixed DEV set, compare enabled and disabled negation handling, separately count outcomes for examples containing negation cues, and verify total quality delta against the threshold.
candidates.rationale: A targeted, bounded polarity rule is feasible in `solution.py` and addresses a stated potential error class without changing the task or evaluator.
candidates.uncertainty: The supplied experiment evidence contains no error breakdown, so it does not show whether negation confusion occurs in DEV.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a lightweight order-sensitive phrase or adjacent-token feature to the matcher in `solution.py`; this will improve exact-match quality if the current bag-of-words overlap confuses concepts with similar words in different compositional orders.
hypothesis.rationale: The authoritative TASK.md names compositional word order as a potential error class. Prior experiments adjust lexical overlap and tie resolution but do not test whether token sequence carries needed meaning.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Quality increases by at least 0.001 versus the current champion, with gains concentrated in statements whose token sets are similar but order differs.
hypothesis.falsification_condition: Reject if the fixed DEV quality delta is below 0.001 or order-sensitive examples show no improvement over the order-insensitive matcher.
hypothesis.novelty_rationale: This tests sequence composition as a new mechanism family. The measured partial gains for experiments 1–3 (0.0002, 0.0003, 0.0004) show incremental overlap-based improvements but not promotion; they do not test or rule out order sensitivity.

candidates.suspected_failure_mode: A bag-of-words score may conflate statements that share terms but differ in phrase order and thus in engineering meaning.
candidates.predicted_observable: Order-sensitive cases become more accurately distinguished and total quality improves by at least 0.001 on the fixed DEV set.
candidates.discriminating_test: Compare an order-sensitive feature against the existing order-insensitive score on the same DEV set; measure total quality and the subset with similar token sets but differing order.
candidates.rationale: This directly challenges the bag-of-words framing while staying within the editable matcher and can be evaluated as a bounded ablation.
candidates.uncertainty: There is no supplied DEV error analysis confirming that word-order confusions occur, so benefit is uncertain.
